data.body:
Round-3 plan review corrections applied, all three blocking findings addressed:

1. AC1 venv contradiction: AC1 listed 'the venv' in the allow-list while the shipped code deliberately EXCLUDES sys.prefix (a writable venv would let a mutant drop executable code into site-packages for a later un-sandboxed phase to import). AC1 now describes the shipped allow-list and states the exclusion reason. The code was right; the criterion was wrong.

2. Incomplete subprocess enumeration: the scoping section now names _diagnose_non_killed (line 660) as a THIRD mutant-executing site that re-runs surviving mutants unsandboxed, explicitly out of scope here and tracked as 724c-b5fd-efb1-40d5.

3. AC11's unverified HOME claim: confirmed empirically before fixing. Deleting 'env = mutation_sandbox.sandbox_env(env)' from execute_shard left all 70 tests green (28 sandbox + 42 gate) because the only HOME test asserted on the mapping sandbox_env returns, never on a child. Gerrit change 2274 adds three tests: two that run a real child and assert the HOME it observes (one unsandboxed so it also covers the Linux cells where probe() returns None and every @live test skips, one through wrap()), and one call-site binding test tying both sandbox-wrapped _run calls to the hardened env.

All three proven RED by real mutation, not asserted: deleting the sandbox_env call fails the binding test; pointing HOMELESS at an existing path fails both child tests; passing a wrapped subprocess the unhardened env fails the binding test. 73 tests green, make lint and make typecheck clean.
